content_metadata.description: A detailed exploration of the history, types, and advancements in telescope technology, focusing on ground-based instruments and the Hubble Space Telescope.

qAndA.answer: A refracting telescope uses a lens (objective lens) to gather and focus light, while a reflecting telescope uses a mirror (concave mirror) to achieve the same purpose.
qAndA.question: What is the main difference between a refracting telescope and a reflecting telescope?

qAndA.answer: A photometer is used to measure the intensity of light coming from celestial objects.
qAndA.question: What is the purpose of a photometer in astronomy?

qAndA.answer: The Hubble Space Telescope orbits above Earth's atmosphere, which eliminates the blurring and distortion caused by atmospheric turbulence. Additionally, it is not affected by light pollution, allowing for clearer and more detailed observations.
qAndA.question: Why is the Hubble Space Telescope considered superior to Earth-based telescopes?

qAndA.answer: The Hubble Space Telescope was launched on April 24th, 1990, aboard the Space Shuttle Discovery.
qAndA.question: When was the Hubble Space Telescope launched into space?

qAndA.answer: A Newtonian reflector utilizes a secondary flat mirror placed near the focal point of the primary concave mirror. This secondary mirror reflects the light out to the side of the telescope where the eyepiece is located.
qAndA.question: How does a Newtonian reflector direct the image to the eyepiece?

text_to_speech: [MUSIC PLAYING] Today's telescopes employ optics similar to those Galileo and Newton originally used centuries ago. Galileo's simple astronomical telescope will remind you of the spyglasses you'd see in pirate movies, or even something you owned as a kid. This refracting telescope uses a main lens at the front called the objective, and a lens at the back called the eyepiece. The eyepiece focuses the light from the objective for your eyes. This telescope design is called the refractor, or refracting telescope. Sir Isaac Newton designed and built a different type of telescope that used a concave mirror as the primary, instead of a lens. Think of the cosmetic mirrors found in many of our homes. The surface is a concave curved shape. And as you look at the mirror, your face looks larger. Incoming light is reflected from this concave mirror back to the front of the telescope. This telescope design is called the reflector, or the reflecting telescope. Different types of reflectors use additional mirrors and lenses. The Newtonian reflector, still the most popular telescope used by professional and amateur astronomers today, uses a second flat mirror to reflect the image to the side of the telescope. At that point the eyepiece can be used to focus the light, much like the refracting telescope. Astronomers don't always look through the microscope. In the place of the eyepiece a number of instruments can be substituted. A camera or charge coupled device can be used to take a photo or image an object. A photo meter will allow the astronomer to determine the amount of light incoming and if that light varies. And a spectroscope can be used to determine the chemical makeup of stars. NASA's Hubble Space Telescope, named after American astronomer Edwin Hubble, was designed to operate in low Earth orbit. The space shuttle Discovery carried it into space on April 24th, 1990. And it will hopefully remain in operation until 2020. A number of aerospace visionaries long dreamed of a space telescope, including Hermann Oberth, Robert Goddard, and Konstantin Tsiolkovsky, as presented in "The Rocket to Planetary Space" in 1923. In 1946 American astronomer Lyman Spitzer suggested an on orbit telescope would be superior to an Earth based telescope due to the fact that an on orbit telescope would be above the atmosphere and light pollution. This would allow an orbital telescope to distinguish finer detail and see fainter objects. Hubble's observations and imaging have produced a new spectacular view of our universe. From our solar system to the faintest objects, Hubble has changed our views of the universe. [MUSIC PLAYING]
